panels.description: Per time bucket, unions issue creation events (by creator) and DONE resolution events (by assignee) and counts each side.

targets.rawSql:
WITH ev AS (
  SELECT i.created_date AS ts, 1 AS opened, 0 AS closed
  FROM issues i
  JOIN board_issues bi ON i.id = bi.issue_id
    AND bi.board_id in ( ${repo_id} )
  JOIN project_mapping pm 
    ON pm.row_id = bi.board_id
    AND pm.table = 'repos'
    AND pm.project_name IN ( ${project} )
  WHERE i.id LIKE 'github:%'
    AND (i.assignee_id IN ( $developer_id ) OR (i.assignee_id IS NULL AND 'unassigned' IN ( $developer_id )))
    AND $__timeFilter(i.created_date)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT i.resolution_date, 0, 1
  FROM issues i
  JOIN board_issues bi ON i.id = bi.issue_id
    AND bi.board_id in ( ${repo_id} )
  JOIN project_mapping pm 
    ON pm.row_id = bi.board_id
    AND pm.table = 'repos'
    AND pm.project_name IN ( ${project} )
  WHERE i.id LIKE 'github:%'
    AND i.status = 'DONE'
    AND i.resolution_date IS NOT NULL
    AND $__timeFilter(i.created_date)
    AND (i.assignee_id IN ( $developer_id ) OR (i.assignee_id IS NULL AND 'unassigned' IN ( $developer_id )))
)
SELECT $__timeGroup(ts, $interval)                                        AS time,
       SUM(opened)                                                   AS Opened,
       SUM(closed)                                                   AS Closed
FROM ev
GROUP BY time
ORDER BY time;

panels.title: Created VS Closed Trend

panels.description: Per time bucket, counts issues created by category after mapping original_type into fixed buckets via keyword matching. This is keyword matching on the raw GitHub issue type/label text, not the connection's scope-config regex -- a repo whose labels don't literally contain a bucket's keyword will show 0 for that category even though the issues exist.

targets.rawSql:
WITH type_map AS (
  SELECT original_type,
         CASE
           WHEN original_type LIKE '%bug%'
             OR original_type LIKE '%issue%'         THEN 'Bugs'
           WHEN original_type LIKE '%documentation%' THEN 'Documentation'
           WHEN original_type LIKE '%R&D%'           THEN 'R&D'
           WHEN original_type LIKE '%review%'        THEN 'Reviews'
           WHEN original_type LIKE '%refactor%'
             OR original_type LIKE '%debt%'
             OR original_type LIKE '%enhancement%'
             OR original_type LIKE '%improvement%'   THEN 'Refactoring'
           WHEN original_type LIKE '%task%'          THEN 'Tasks'
           ELSE 'Other'
         END AS category
  FROM (SELECT DISTINCT original_type FROM issues) d
)
SELECT $__timeGroup(i.created_date, $interval)     AS time,
       SUM(tm.category = 'Bugs')              AS Bugs,
       SUM(tm.category = 'Refactoring')       AS Refactoring,
       SUM(tm.category = 'Tasks')             AS Tasks,
       SUM(tm.category = 'Documentation')     AS Documentation,
       SUM(tm.category = 'R&D')               AS `R&D`,
       SUM(tm.category = 'Reviews')           AS Reviews,
       SUM(tm.category = 'Other')             AS Unclassified
FROM issues i
JOIN type_map tm ON tm.original_type <=> i.original_type
JOIN accounts a ON a.id = i.assignee_id AND a.id IN ( $developer_id )
WHERE i.id LIKE 'github:%'
  AND $__timeFilter(i.created_date)
GROUP BY time
ORDER BY time;

panels.title: Issue Type Mix Trend

panels.description: Per mapped issue type and priority, derives median and P75 of lead_time_minutes in days for DONE issues, keeping groups with at least 3 issues.

targets.rawSql:
WITH type_map AS (
  SELECT original_type,
         CASE
           WHEN original_type LIKE '%bug%'
             OR original_type LIKE '%issue%'         THEN 'Bugs'
           WHEN original_type LIKE '%documentation%' THEN 'Documentation'
           WHEN original_type LIKE '%R&D%'           THEN 'R&D'
           WHEN original_type LIKE '%review%'        THEN 'Reviews'
           WHEN original_type LIKE '%refactor%'
             OR original_type LIKE '%debt%'
             OR original_type LIKE '%enhancement%'
             OR original_type LIKE '%improvement%'   THEN 'Refactoring'
           WHEN original_type LIKE '%task%'          THEN 'Tasks'
           ELSE 'Unclassified Issues'
         END AS category
  FROM (SELECT DISTINCT original_type FROM issues) d
),
d AS (
  SELECT tm.category                                        AS type,
         COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(i.priority), ''), '(none)')   AS priority,
         i.lead_time_minutes / 1440.0                       AS days
  FROM issues i
  JOIN type_map tm ON tm.original_type <=> i.original_type
  JOIN accounts a ON a.id = i.assignee_id AND a.id IN ( $developer_id )
  WHERE i.status = 'DONE'
    AND i.lead_time_minutes IS NOT NULL
    AND i.lead_time_minutes > 0
    AND i.id LIKE 'github:%'
    AND $__timeFilter(i.resolution_date)
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT type, priority, days,
         CUME_DIST() OVER (PARTITION BY type, priority ORDER BY days) AS cd
  FROM d
)
SELECT type AS Type,
       priority AS Priority,
       COUNT(*)                                            AS `Total Issues`,
       ROUND(MIN(CASE WHEN cd >= 0.50 THEN days END), 1)  AS `Median Days`,
       ROUND(MIN(CASE WHEN cd >= 0.75 THEN days END), 1)  AS `P75 Days`
FROM ranked
GROUP BY type, priority
HAVING `Total Issues` >= 3
ORDER BY type, `Median Days` DESC;

panels.title: Issue Lead Time

panels.description: Lists open issues not updated in over 14 days with their assignee and days since the last update.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT REPLACE(COALESCE(
         NULLIF(TRIM(a.full_name),     ''),
         NULLIF(TRIM(a.user_name),     ''),
         NULLIF(TRIM(i.assignee_name), ''),
         '(unassigned)'
       ), '-', ' ') AS Developer, 
  i.title AS Issue,
  DATEDIFF(CURDATE(), i.updated_date) AS `Lead Time Days`
FROM issues i
JOIN accounts a ON a.id = i.assignee_id AND a.id IN ( $developer_id )
WHERE i.id LIKE 'github:%'
  AND i.original_status = 'OPEN'
  AND DATEDIFF(CURDATE(), i.updated_date) > 14
  AND $__timeFilter(i.updated_date) 
ORDER BY `Lead Time Days` DESC

list.definition:
select DISTINCT upm.project_name
from user_project_mapping upm 
join project_mapping pm ON upm.project_name = pm.project_name 
WHERE pm.`table` = 'repos' AND pm.row_id like 'github:%'
and upm.user_login = ${__user.login:sqlstring}
ORDER BY upm.project_name

FROM project_mapping pm 
JOIN repos r ON r.id = pm.row_id

AND pm.project_name IN ( $project )

list.definition:
WITH scoped_repos AS (
  SELECT r.id
  FROM repos r
  WHERE r.id LIKE 'github:%'
    AND r.deleted = 0
    AND r.id IN ( ${repo_id} )
    AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM project_mapping pm
                 WHERE pm.row_id  = r.id
                   AND pm.`table` = 'repos'
                   AND pm.project_name IN ( ${project} ))
),
scoped_accounts AS (
  -- PR authors
  SELECT pr.author_id AS account_id
  FROM pull_requests pr
  JOIN scoped_repos sr ON sr.id = pr.base_repo_id
  WHERE pr.author_id LIKE 'github:%'
  UNION
  -- reviewers and commenters
  SELECT cmt.account_id
  FROM pull_request_comments cmt
  JOIN pull_requests pr ON pr.id = cmt.pull_request_id
  JOIN scoped_repos sr  ON sr.id = pr.base_repo_id
  WHERE cmt.account_id LIKE 'github:%'
  UNION
  -- issue assignees, scoped through boards (github board ids match repo ids)
  SELECT ia.assignee_id
  FROM issue_assignees ia
  JOIN board_issues bi ON bi.issue_id = ia.issue_id
  WHERE ia.assignee_id LIKE 'github:%'
    AND bi.board_id IN ( ${repo_id} )
    AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM project_mapping pm
                 WHERE pm.row_id  = bi.board_id
                   AND pm.`table` = 'boards'
                   AND pm.project_name IN ( ${project} ))
)
SELECT Name FROM (
  SELECT CONCAT(
           REPLACE(COALESCE(
             NULLIF(TRIM(a.full_name), ''),
             NULLIF(TRIM(a.user_name), ''),
             NULLIF(TRIM(a.email),     ''),
             '(unmapped)'
           ), '-', ' '),
           '--', a.id) AS Name
  FROM accounts a
  JOIN scoped_accounts sa ON sa.account_id = a.id
  GROUP BY Name
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Unassigned--unassigned'
) all_developers
ORDER BY Name
